label: token right after a b at sequence position 1 or 2
explanation: Fires during the original phase on the step right after a b input, but only when that b is original token 0 or 1 (so the feature fires at t=1 or t=2). Which token comes after the b makes no difference. Magnitude depends on position: when b is the first token (t=1) activations are near max (~3.3-3.4). When b is the second token (t=2) they are about 0.4-0.6 of max, so t=1 carries ~68% of the mass even though active counts at t=1 and t=2 are about equal. It does not fire after a b later in the sequence (t>=3 is almost never active), in the delimiter or copy phase (including when b is fed back during the copy), or after any other token.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split there are 0 false positives and 116 missed active steps holding 0.0% of activation mass. The misses are tiny (0.00-0.07 of max), mostly at t=3 right after a t=2 'b' (e.g. 'x b b ...'), plus a few copy-phase blips. This is scattered, near-zero noise.

Position claims hold on test. t==1 alone: P=1.0, R=0.50, mass recall 0.68, which matches the ~68% mass claim. Its activations fill the top two activation quartiles, so near max. The t=2 activations sit in the second quartile, around 0.5 of max per the misses rendering ([b:0.51]). Widening to t<=3 gives F1=0.802, which matches the claimed 0.80.

On the dev profile, phase claims hold: 0 activations at the delimiter, 34 of 33431 active steps in the copy phase (0.000 mass), and 0 at t=0. By-input-token activation rates are flat (~0.006 for every token), consistent with 'which token comes after the b makes no difference'.

Minor wording point: 'b at sequence position 1 or 2' in the label means the step after the b is at t=1 or 2, not that the b itself is at position 1 or 2. The explanation states this correctly. Not an overclaim.
